Definition: perhaps remotely from χέω (to shed forth); chaff (as diffusive):--chaff.
BiblicalUsage: Chaff — achyron is the husk the wind carries away. John the Baptist preached it twice over: the Christ "will throughly purge his floor, and gather his wheat into the garner; but he will burn up the chaff with unquenchable fire." The picture is the threshing floor: wheat kept, chaff burned.
TheologicalSignificance: Chaff is farm imagery, and the judgment it pictures is the point — the wind keeps the wheat and carries the husk away.
